findings.description: Only a moved events-file mtime stops the next hold, and a hold moves it only when its turn's Stop hook fires. A hold whose turn dies (API error, no Stop) or runs past one sweep is typed again every 15 s, which can spend all eight holds in about two minutes.
findings.body:
**Concern.** After a hold is submitted, only the events file's mtime keeps the next sweep from holding the same window again. The worker profile appends to that file only on `PostToolUse`, `Stop` and `Notification` (`src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts` L1163-1171). It has no `UserPromptSubmit` entry, and `pasteIntoPane`/`submitPane` only send tmux keys. So the mtime stays put until the hold's own turn fires a hook.

On the next sweep (`WATCH_INTERVAL_MS` = 15 s, `src/core/overlap.service.ts` L12), every check in `holdDue` passes again:
- `idleMs` is unchanged and still inside [50, 58) min.
- `trailingHolds` is 1, which is below `CACHE_HOLD_LIMIT`. The recorded `cache_hold` is never compared with the mtime.
- The tail still ends on the earlier Stop, so `classifySessionActivity` says `idle`.
- `readInputBox` returns `'empty'`, both while a turn runs and after a turn dies.

**Triggers.**
1. The hold's turn dies with an API error. A dead turn fires no Stop (`turn-watchdog.service.ts` L30-35). An `awaiting-review` window then gets a hold typed every 15 s until the cap is spent, which takes about two minutes.
2. The hold's turn takes longer than one sweep interval. A second hold queues behind the first, and the cap is counted twice for one refresh.

The catch comment at L94-95 ("A hold typed but left unrecorded moved the events file") rests on the same wrong assumption. `src/cli/index.ts` L1976-1977 says the events file only moves on the next hook. No test sweeps twice over an unchanged mtime.

**Fix.** Treat a hold whose `cache_hold` row is at or after the file's mtime as still unanswered:

```ts
const [newest] = events;
if (newest?.type === 'cache_hold' && Date.parse(toIsoUtc(newest.created_at)) >= stat.mtimeMs) return undefined;
```

This needs `toIsoUtc` from `./report-data.utils.js`. Add a repeat-sweep test with it.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/7201627eb3cb2b3500c37c4e043bd696bfe6e8c5/src/core/cache-hold.service.ts#L118-L123

findings.description: A hold is typed into a turn that is already running, because typing a prompt never moves the events file. Three cases: the hold's own turn, a just-recorded steer or peer message, or a resume from the same sweep.
findings.body:
**Concern.** `holdDue` takes "the hook events show the turn ended" as proven when the file's mtime is in the window and the tail ends on a Stop. Only the PostToolUse, Stop and Notification hooks write that file (`profile-compiler.service.ts` L1163-1171). A turn that has started therefore writes nothing until its first tool finishes or it stops.

The input box is still drawn while a turn runs, which is why `steerPane` can steer mid-turn (`session-runtime.service.ts` L1233). So `readInputBox` returns `'empty'` (see `inputBoxState` in `src/claude/pane.utils.ts` L158-167), and the paste plus Enter queues into that turn.

**A just-recorded steer or peer message (the main case).** An `awaiting-review` worker has been quiet for 52 minutes. A conductor `pup steer` or a peer message (`recordSteerMessage`) wakes it, and it starts a long `pnpm test`. A steer only adds a DB row. It does not move the file, and it resets `trailingHolds` to 0. `awaiting-review` needs no open question. So any 15 s sweep before that tool's PostToolUse queues "Run no tool; reply with the single word held and end your turn" into the real working turn.

**The same sweep's resume.** `sweepDeadTurns` runs `resumeSession` and then `holdIdleCaches` with the same `now` (`turn-watchdog.service.ts` L92-96). A file quiet for 50 to 58 minutes is past the stall threshold. So a `running` worker with an open question can be resumed and then held straight away, when its dead turn wrote no hook events.

This breaks ADR 0179's promise that a hold "is made only when the hook events show the turn ended" (`docs/adr/0179-…md` L27).

**Fix.** Also skip when something that types into the pane was recorded after the file last moved. `events` is already newest-first here:

```ts
const typed = events.find((e) => ['steer', 'answer', 'interrupt', 'cache_hold'].includes(e.type));
if (typed && Date.parse(toIsoUtc(typed.created_at)) >= stat.mtimeMs) return undefined;
```

This also closes the previous finding's re-hold path.

findings.description: A hold whose turn dies on an API error turns a worker waiting on an open question into a watchdog resume target. The watchdog then types RESUME_MESSAGE ("Continue the task ... run pup session done") while the question is still open.
findings.body:
**Concern.** Before this PR, a `running` worker whose ask turn ended normally could not show a dead turn: nothing typed into its pane, so `deadTurnError` found no API-error line and `resumeSession` left it alone. `holdIdleCaches` now starts a turn in exactly those panes.

Suppose that hold turn dies (DNS outage, lost connection; the failure the watchdog exists for):
1. No Stop fires, and the session stalls (`findStalledSessions` lists `running` rows quiet 10 min or more).
2. No `turn_died` exists for that `stalledAt`. Nothing was recorded at the earlier 10-minute mark, because that turn ended cleanly.
3. The pane now ends on the API-error line, so the next sweep's `resumeSession` (L108-155) types `RESUME_MESSAGE`: "Continue the task from where you stopped and run pup session done when the acceptance criteria are met."

`resumeSession` never reads `openQuestion`. Its steer is recorded `by: 'watch'`, and `openQuestion` (`session.repository.ts` L713) ignores any steer whose `by` is not `'operator'`. So the question stays open in Needs-you while the worker is told to finish without the answer it asked for.

This contradicts ADR 0179's statement that only the operator answers a question a hold leaves open. The ADR's amendment of 0035 covers only the stall age resetting, not this new resume path. Fixing the re-hold check in `holdDue` does not prevent it, because one dead hold is enough.

**Fix.** In `resumeSession`, do not resume a dead turn that belongs to a hold. For example, skip (or record a `turn_died` and type nothing) when the newest `cache_hold`/`steer` event is a `cache_hold`, or when the session has an open question.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/7201627eb3cb2b3500c37c4e043bd696bfe6e8c5/src/core/turn-watchdog.service.ts#L92-L96

findings.description: ADR 0179 declares `Amends: 0035`, but 0035's header still lists only `Amended by: 0103`, so a reader of 0035 won't learn that a hold now restarts the stall age; add the `Amended by: [0179](…)` back-link as sibling pairs like 0078→0036 do.

The file header and the CACHE_HOLD_LIMIT JSDoc restate ADR 0179's cost figures: the retro date, 93 re-caches, about 84 USD, and the 0.1× vs 2× arithmetic. These copies go stale when either side changes. Cut the header to a pointer to decision 179, and keep only the "cost control, not a boundary" WHY on the limit.

holdDue loads and reverses the session's whole event list before the cheaper openQuestion early return; moving the running/open-question check above `listEvents` skips that load for running sessions with no question.

readTail's short-read loop (`-1` sentinel, running offset) guards a case a regular file only hits when it shrinks mid-read, which just yields a shorter tail the classifier tolerates; a single `readSync(fd, buffer, 0, buffer.length, start)` would do, or a comment should name the case the loop covers.
